first.rationale: Current state shows onboarding completion down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ. memory_31 and memory_86 document that signup/onboarding simplification produced durable lifts in first-week activation and completion rates. This directly addresses both declining metrics and is the highest-leverage lever available. Competitive pressure on price-sensitive SMBs (memory_73) is real, but acquisition via cheaper pricing without fixing onboarding/activation funnel efficiency wastes CAC and worsens unit economics. memory_86 (onboarding completion lift) is verified because the current 4% decline suggests the prior gains may have regressed or new friction was introduced. memory_73 (promotional pricing) is verified to confirm its magnitude and SMB segment specificity before considering it as a follow-up experiment if activation simplification proves insufficient. Simplifying onboarding is a lower-risk, faster-iterating lever than enterprise sales assist (which requires sales hiring and is orthogonal to core product metrics) and safer than referral incentives when core funnel health is declining. Standard experiment scale allows controlled measurement while preserving capacity for competitive response if needed.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms memory_86: onboarding simplification yields +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% retention. This is a durable, sustainable lever. Critically, exp_73 reveals that targeted promotional pricing achieves +31% signup and +18% revenue but destroys retention (-12%), failing to deliver qualified revenue long-term. The competitor's aggressive pricing is therefore a distraction from fundamentals. Current state shows 4% onboarding completion decline and 6% activation decline QoQ—both directly addressable by repeating the proven simplification playbook. The -12% retention penalty on discounted SMB cohorts means competing on price alone accelerates churn and worsens lifetime value. Simplifying onboarding is the only candidate that durably improves both acquisition efficiency and retention while addressing both current metrics failures. Standard experiment scale is appropriate for validating repeatability. This decision preserves long-term unit economics and qualified revenue.
